summary: Two complementary research leads were verified. CMS QualityNet provides current PSI specifications and public reporting context relevant to the existing CMS safety measures. HCUP NIS can support a national inpatient-stay benchmark, but its post-2012 design does not support hospital-specific totals and access requires training and a data-use agreement; under the stated constraints it is a discovery lead, not an available acquisition. No new New Brunswick- or Middlesex County-specific dataset was verified in this bounded search.

sources.title: Patient Safety Indicators (PSI) resources
sources.publisher: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, QualityNet
sources.geography: United States; hospital-specific CMS reporting context, not a Middlesex County-specific extract
sources.period: Current resource page includes reporting-period and version details; for example, October 2025 public reporting and FY 2026 HAC Reduction Program use PSI software v15.0 and a 24-month discharge period of 2023-07-01 to 2025-06-30
sources.grain: Measure specifications and program-level reporting guidance; linked public materials describe hospital-level PSI results and methods
useful_fields: PSI measure identifiers and technical specifications
observed_facts: CMS states that public PSI reporting continues although PSI 90 was removed from the IQR program for FY 2020 onward.
The page provides technical specifications, fact sheets, risk-adjustment reports and reporting-period/version information.
CMS states that PSI software for replicating hospital results is available by request and is not publicly posted; the linked specifications and explanatory documents are public.
sources.retrieval_next_step: For a bounded follow-up, identify the current PSI version and technical specification files applicable to each target measure, then map measure numerator, denominator, exclusions, risk adjustment, reporting window and suppression rules against the ten already acquired measures. Use the CMS public data catalog only if adding an actual hospital-level result extract; preserve each measure's reporting period and population.
limitations: This is methodological documentation and does not itself provide a newly verified direct data download for RWJUH CCN 310038 or Saint Peter's CCN 310070.
Do not treat a risk-adjusted measure or composite as an individual patient outcome or as a local event count.
Version and reporting windows vary by program and release; do not combine versions without documenting the change.

sources.title: Checklist for Working with the National Inpatient Sample (NIS)
sources.publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, Healthcare Cost and Utilization Project
sources.geography: United States national community-hospital inpatient sample
sources.period: Annual database releases; this checked page does not establish a particular downloadable data vintage
sources.grain: Inpatient stay; not patient-level longitudinal records. Since 2012, sample design does not support hospital-level totals; it can support some hospital percentages and national estimates with weights.
useful_fields: discharge weight DISCWT for 2012 onward national estimates
diagnosis/procedure grouping fields in applicable vintages
observed_facts: AHRQ says access requires completing HCUP Data Use Agreement training and reading/signing the Nationwide Database Data Use Agreement.
The NIS sampling design does not support state-level estimates or hospital-level totals for 2012 onward; users must not attempt to identify individual facilities.
The unit is inpatient stays, and the data do not include patient identifiers or support patient tracking.
sources.retrieval_next_step: Treat this only as an external national benchmark lead. If a later authorized collection permits the required training and DUA, select a documented NIS vintage, obtain its accompanying documentation, use design weights for national estimates, and define a pooled national case-mix benchmark at inpatient-stay grain. Do not identify or estimate outcomes for either New Brunswick hospital from NIS.
limitations: Not a local hospital or county estimate and unsuitable for facility-level benchmarking in the current post-2012 design.
The data-use agreement and training are outside the authorized scope of this task; no data were acquired.
Sampling design, coding, and available variables differ by vintage; a single assumed source version must not be used.

missing_inputs: No additional verified public quantitative extract specific to RWJUH CCN 310038, Saint Peter's CCN 310070, or Middlesex County was established in this bounded search.

For the existing ten safety/outcome records, the measure-level denominator, unit, risk adjustment, confidence bounds and suppression metadata still require review against their specific source specifications.
simulation_use: Use QualityNet specifications to interpret and qualify the existing CMS safety/outcome measures and preserve measure version, population, reporting window, adjustment and suppression information. Any hospital-level risk-adjusted rate or SIR may be an external benchmark or calibration reference only; it must not determine an individual synthetic patient's outcome. NIS is a potential national inpatient-stay benchmark only if a separate authorized data-access process is later approved.
limitations: Search scope was limited to two web searches and four official-page opens; absence of a verified local source here does not establish that none exists.
This is candidate-source research, not acquisition, calibration, or independent domain-owner approval.
